all_body_units.old_text: # Benin SARL and SA formation working paper v0.2

> **General reference only.** This skill is general tax/accounting reference material for AI-assisted workflows. It has not been reviewed for any specific person's facts, documents, elections, deadlines, residency, filing status, or local procedures. Do not rely on it to file, pay, amend, or take a tax position without review by a qualified professional in the relevant jurisdiction.
## Who this applies to

Prepare the registration and capital checklist for an ordinary Benin SARL/SUARL or SA in 2026, with other forms referred to their own legal and APIEx requirements. APIEx's portal lists SARL, SA, SAS, SUARL, SNC, SCS and GIE; a sole-trader establishment and branch are separate choices, not interchangeable company forms. This Guide prepares the packet and capital/fee comparison. It does not submit an authenticated registration or determine a regulated-activity licence. [APIEx](https://monentreprise.bj/creer/societe) [AUSCGIE, art. 309](https://biblio.ohada.org/doc_num.php?explnum_id=2032)

The signed national SARL decree is dated **26 March 2014**, despite the portal link label saying 28 March. Its article 6 permits freely determined capital; OHADA article 311 expressly allows contrary national provisions. Use the signed text, not the obsolete regional default as a mandatory Benin SARL minimum. [AUSCGIE, art. 311](https://biblio.ohada.org/doc_num.php?explnum_id=2032) [Decree 2014-220, arts. 6 and 11](https://monentreprise.bj/Decret_N_2014_220_du_28_mars_2014_portant_modalites_de_creation_des_Societes_a_Responsabilite_Limitee_a73a58faf6.pdf#page=3)
## Rates, bands and thresholds

| Item | Rule and conditions | Official source |
|---|---|---|
| SARL capital | Freely set by the associates in the statutes; not a registration fee | [Decree 2014-220, art. 6](https://monentreprise.bj/Decret_N_2014_220_du_28_mars_2014_portant_modalites_de_creation_des_Societes_a_Responsabilite_Limitee_a73a58faf6.pdf#page=3) |
| SARL cash subscription | At least half paid at subscription; balance within two years of RCCM registration. In-kind contributions paid in full | [AUSCGIE, art. 311-1](https://biblio.ohada.org/doc_num.php?explnum_id=2032) |
| SA minimum capital | FCFA 10 million, fully subscribed; cash shares at least one quarter paid at subscription, balance within three years after RCCM registration | [AUSCGIE, art. 387](https://biblio.ohada.org/doc_num.php?explnum_id=2032); [AUSCGIE, art. 388](https://biblio.ohada.org/doc_num.php?explnum_id=2032); [AUSCGIE, art. 389](https://biblio.ohada.org/doc_num.php?explnum_id=2032) |
| Published APIEx SARL/SUARL fee | FCFA 22,000; notary/professional charges not included | [APIEx](https://monentreprise.bj/informer/couts-delais); [APIEx](https://monentreprise.bj/creer/societe) |
| Published APIEx SA/SAS fee | FCFA 37,000; notary/professional charges not included | [APIEx](https://monentreprise.bj/informer/couts-delais); [APIEx](https://monentreprise.bj/creer/societe) |
| Published processing target | Three working hours after a complete submission; a service target, not a guarantee that an incomplete or regulated case is complete | [APIEx](https://monentreprise.bj/creer/societe) |
| SARL statutory auditor | At least two: balance-sheet total over FCFA 125 million; annual turnover over FCFA 250 million; permanent staff over 50. Judicial appointment can also be requested by associates holding at least one tenth of capital | [AUSCGIE, art. 376](https://biblio.ohada.org/doc_num.php?explnum_id=2032) |
| SA statutory auditor | Mandatory control by one or more statutory auditors | [AUSCGIE, art. 694](https://biblio.ohada.org/doc_num.php?explnum_id=2032) |
## The base

1. Choose the legal form from the ownership, liability, governance, financing and regulated-activity facts. A SARL can have one or several associates with liability limited to contributions. Do not treat a branch or sole trader as a company with identical capital/liability. [AUSCGIE, art. 309](https://biblio.ohada.org/doc_num.php?explnum_id=2032) [APIEx](https://monentreprise.bj/creer/societe)
2. Separate subscribed capital, paid capital, the remaining payment obligation, the government registration fee and professional charges. SARL cash funds are deposited in an authorised bank/credit/microfinance institution with a receipt in the formation company's name; record the payment/deposit in the statutes. [AUSCGIE, art. 311-1](https://biblio.ohada.org/doc_num.php?explnum_id=2032) [Decree arts. 7–8](https://monentreprise.bj/Decret_N_2014_220_du_28_mars_2014_portant_modalites_de_creation_des_Societes_a_Responsabilite_Limitee_a73a58faf6.pdf#page=3)
3. Prepare statutes signed by all associates, identity documents for associates/managers, the manager's criminal-record extract, head-office domiciliation evidence, SA/SAS subscription/payment declaration and cash-deposit certificate where applicable. APIEx requires a notary for SA/SAS; SARL statutes can be private or notarised. Confirm the specific document list for foreigners and in-kind contributions before submission. [APIEx](https://monentreprise.bj/creer/societe) [Decree art. 2](https://monentreprise.bj/Decret_N_2014_220_du_28_mars_2014_portant_modalites_de_creation_des_Societes_a_Responsabilite_Limitee_a73a58faf6.pdf#page=2)
4. Test statutory-auditor requirements against the law's two-of-three SARL test and the separate SA rule. Do not use the portal comparison's capital-based/any-one test in place of OHADA article 376. Review appointment/release procedures separately for a live case. [AUSCGIE, art. 376](https://biblio.ohada.org/doc_num.php?explnum_id=2032) [AUSCGIE, art. 694](https://biblio.ohada.org/doc_num.php?explnum_id=2032)
## Deadlines and filing

Start at [APIEx MonEntreprise](https://monentreprise.bj/creer/societe), select the actual form and prepare the stated documents. The public process describes an online form, online payment, APIEx processing with the tribunal/DGI/CNSS and downloadable certificates. The authenticated fields, checkout, final validation and receipts were not accessed; this working paper stops before submission. [APIEx](https://monentreprise.bj/informer/processus)

Reconcile the received RCCM extract, IFU tax identifier, CNSS employer notification, labour declaration and legal announcement against the application. Check their authenticity using the portal's certificate instructions. IFU is the DGI-assigned identifier; do not substitute a guessed tax number. [APIEx](https://monentreprise.bj/informer/certificats)

For continuing ordinary-company compliance, maintain the applicable OHADA accounts and the annual IS attachment pack, use the [corporate Guide](bj-corporate-income-tax.md) for tax filing dates, and the [VAT](bj-vat-gst.md) and [payroll](bj-payroll-social.md) Guides when those obligations apply. The annual accounts meeting is required within six months of exercise close under article 140; account filing and any extension need their actual procedure. [CGI 2026, art. 50](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=30) [AUSCGIE, art. 140](https://biblio.ohada.org/doc_num.php?explnum_id=2032)
## Penalties and interest

This packet does not price registration, corporate-law or professional failures from memory. Obtain the applicable sanction provision and notice for a live failure. Tax filing/payment sanctions are separately recorded in the [overview](bj-tax-overview.md#penalties-and-interest).
## Cross-border points

Foreign associates, a foreign manager and a branch require the actual identity, residence and parent-entity documents. Benin registration does not decide the foreign parent's PE or treaty outcome, nor automatically licence a regulated activity. Tax PE and withholding must be tested separately. [APIEx](https://monentreprise.bj/informer/pieces-requises) [CGI 2026, art. 5](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=9) [CGI 2026, art. 6](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=10)
## Two worked examples that recompute

**SARL paid capital and registration fee are different amounts.** Assume the associates choose FCFA 2 million in cash capital and use the minimum half-payment at subscription. Paid capital is 1 million, unpaid capital is 1 million and the published APIEx fee is 22,000. Initial identified funding is 1,022,000 before professional costs, not 2,022,000 and not a claim that the whole capital is a fee.

```oa-check
name: SARL capital versus fee
inputs:
  subscribed_cash_capital: 2000000
  official_fee: 22000
steps:
  cash_paid_now: subscribed_cash_capital*0.50
  cash_unpaid: subscribed_cash_capital-cash_paid_now
  identified_initial_funding: cash_paid_now+official_fee
expected:
  cash_paid_now: 1000000
  cash_unpaid: 1000000
  identified_initial_funding: 1022000
```

**SA capital decision.** Assume an ordinary SA at the statutory minimum with all contributions in cash. At least one quarter is paid at subscription, so identified paid capital is 2.5 million and the balance is 7.5 million. Add the published 37,000 fee separately; notary/professional costs remain outside the amount. This uses the signed law's quarter rule, not the inconsistent half-capital portal comparison.

```oa-check
name: SA quarter capital payment
inputs:
  subscribed_cash_capital: 10000000
  official_fee: 37000
steps:
  minimum_paid_now: subscribed_cash_capital*0.25
  remaining_cash_capital: subscribed_cash_capital-minimum_paid_now
  identified_initial_funding: minimum_paid_now+official_fee
expected:
  minimum_paid_now: 2500000
  remaining_cash_capital: 7500000
  identified_initial_funding: 2537000
```
## Ask the client first

- Which form, owners, liability/governance needs and regulated activity are proposed?
- Are there foreign owners/managers, a branch or a non-Benin parent?
- What capital is subscribed, in cash/in kind, paid and still due?
- Which signed statutes, identity, criminal-record, address and deposit documents are ready?
- What are the balance sheet, turnover and permanent staff for the auditor test?
- What registration identifiers, certificates, tax regimes and ongoing filing obligations already exist?

# Benin corporate IS working paper v0.2

> **General reference only.** This skill is general tax/accounting reference material for AI-assisted workflows. It has not been reviewed for any specific person's facts, documents, elections, deadlines, residency, filing status, or local procedures. Do not rely on it to file, pay, amend, or take a tax position without review by a qualified professional in the relevant jurisdiction.
## Who this applies to

Prepare the ordinary Benin IS calculation and instalment reconciliation in 2026 using the law applicable to the particular accounting period. SARL, SA and SAS fall within the form-based charge; exemptions, incentives and sector conventions must be checked before this ordinary computation is used. [CGI 2026, art. 3](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=6) [CGI 2026, art. 4](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=7) [CGI 2026, art. 145](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=71) [CGI 2026, art. 146](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=71)

The territorial rule covers enterprises operated in Benin and profits allocated to Benin under a double-tax agreement. Resident entities and non-residents with a permanent establishment are addressed by articles 5–6. Do not assume a foreign branch is automatically outside the computation without checking those conditions. This Guide produces a reviewed calculation schedule, not a completed electronic return. [CGI 2026, art. 5](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=9) [CGI 2026, art. 6](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=10)
## Rates, bands and thresholds

| Item | Rule and conditions | Official source |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary profit rate | 30% of taxable profit for persons other than the 25% group | [CGI 2026, art. 46](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=28) |
| Industrial/private-school rate | 25% for industrial activity excluding extractive industries, and the listed private school, university, technical and professional education entities | [CGI 2026, art. 46](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=28) |
| Mining/petroleum convention | Use the convention rate, which cannot be lower than the applicable ordinary rate; no fixed 35–45% band is asserted | [CGI 2026, art. 46](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=28) |
| Ordinary minimum | 1% of produits encaissables, with an absolute FCFA 250,000 floor; first screen the sector exceptions below | [CGI 2026, art. 47](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=29) |
| Construction/public works minimum | 3% of produits encaissables | [CGI 2026, art. 47](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=29) |
| Property-predominant companies | 10% of produits encaissables, using the article 101 definition | [CGI 2026, art. 47](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=29); [CGI 2026, art. 101](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=54) |
| Used vehicles/certain consumer goods | Separate regulatory minimum; do not use the ordinary formula before that regime is resolved | [CGI 2026, art. 47](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=29) |
| Service stations and specified non-importing petroleum distributors | At least FCFA 0.60 per litre sold and at least FCFA 250,000, under article 47(5) conditions | [CGI 2026, art. 47](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=29) |
| ORTB levy | FCFA 4,000 in addition to IS, payable with the March instalment | [CGI 2026, art. 47](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=29) |
| Loss carry-forward | Up to the fifth year following the loss year, subject to proof, no prior use, same enterprise and the article 43 restrictions | [CGI 2026, art. 43](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=27) |
## The base

1. Start from the accounts and identify the correct taxpayer, period, territorial scope and any exempt income. The ordinary year closes on 31 December; teaching establishments and qualifying first periods have article 8 exceptions. [CGI 2026, art. 8](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=13)
2. Reconcile accounting profit to taxable profit. The net-profit rule is article 9. Deduct only effective business charges of the correct period, sufficiently supported, producing non-exempt income, reducing net assets and, where required, backed by paid withholding. Apply specific expense restrictions separately; this Guide does not certify every adjustment. Fines and penalties within article 36 are non-deductible. [CGI 2026, art. 9](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=13) [CGI 2026, art. 20](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=18) [CGI 2026, art. 36](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=24)
3. Reconcile produits encaissables separately from turnover and taxable profit: include amounts giving or capable of giving a financial flow; exclude capitalised production, inventory production, transfers of charges, and reversals of provisions/depreciation. [CGI 2026, art. 47](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=29)
4. Compare profit-based IS, the applicable sector minimum and the absolute floor. Keep the ORTB levy separate. Route newly created, restructured, art-trading and approved-incentive cases to their specific assessment before finalising. [CGI 2026, art. 46](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=28) [CGI 2026, art. 47](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=29) [CGI 2026, art. 145](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=71) [CGI 2026, art. 146](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=71)
5. Deduct documented instalments and allowable credits once. Record any excess as a credit under article 51 rather than assuming an immediate refund. [CGI 2026, art. 51](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=32)
## Deadlines and filing

The annual result declaration is due by 30 April for the preceding exercise. Attach the article 50 accounts, expense/depreciation/provision schedules and required supporting disclosures. Ordinary accounts use the applicable OHADA presentation; regulated sectors have their own frameworks. [CGI 2026, art. 49](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=30) [CGI 2026, art. 50](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=30)

Four instalments, each normally one quarter of the preceding year's IS, fall due by 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December. The first instalment can use the penultimate year's tax provisionally if the latest return is not yet filed; regularise at the second instalment. Pay the balance with the annual declaration. A reduction of instalments requires the article 52 process, not an informal decision. [CGI 2026, art. 51](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=32) [CGI 2026, art. 52](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=32)

Prepare the calculation and attachment list for the authorised filer on [DGI e-services](https://e-services.impots.bj/). The authenticated form, field mapping, payment reference and acknowledgement were not accessed. Stop before filing until those are confirmed.
## Penalties and interest

General filing/payment sanctions and the conditional 2026 first-declaration relief are recorded once in the [overview](bj-tax-overview.md#penalties-and-interest). Assess the facts before using any relief. This working paper does not prepare a penalty assessment.
## Cross-border points

Cross-border related-party adjustments belong in the [transfer-pricing screen](bj-transfer-pricing.md). Dividend, interest and foreign-service withholding is owned by the [cross-border withholding Guide](bj-cross-border-withholding.md), which includes the 2026 rectifying-law distribution and platform gates. Do not reuse the legacy dividend, listed-company or royalty figures. ## The base

1. Classify the payment: dividend, ordinary interest, bond/security product, royalty/service, rental-platform receipt or a different item. Record the gross contractual amount, accessory costs, currency evidence, expense recognition, interest debit/credit accounting-entry dates and payment/meeting dates. [CGI 2026, art. 85](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=48) [CGI 2026, art. 86](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=48) [CGI 2026, art. 142](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=69)
2. Establish recipient residence, legal form, beneficial ownership and PE facts. For a claimed service/royalty treaty relief, obtain fiscal-residence evidence, beneficial-owner evidence and evidence of liability to corporate/equivalent tax without exemption. Communicate the article 142 information to the administration in the month the charge is recognised. No named-country treaty relief is supplied here without the actual convention. [CGI 2026, art. 142](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=69)
3. Reconcile goods and services. The goods exclusion needs separate invoicing under article 142(4); merely describing a mixed contract as 'equipment' is insufficient. Calculate the withholding on the confirmed base and keep any VAT assessment separate. [CGI 2026, art. 142](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=69)
4. For ordinary dividends and interest, apply their own category, not the foreign-service percentage. For ordinary interest, article 85(2) makes tax due on payment in any form or entry of the interest as a debit or credit in the debtor’s books or the creditor’s account, even when the sums have not yet been paid. Record that tax event separately from the dividend approval and foreign-service expense events; do not defer interest recognition merely because cash has not moved. [CGI 2026, art. 85(2)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=48) Check the approved-exchange condition before a listed-company rate and the specific treaty conditions before any reduction. [CGI 2026, art. 86](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=48) [CGI 2026, art. 88](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=49) [CGI 2026, art. 89](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=49)
5. **Hold special distribution cases for a separate calculation.** LFR articles 3–7 add and define the retained-profit rule, associated tax base/deadline and transitional regularisation. Article 7 sets a reduced 7.5% rate for pre-law undistributed distributable profits regularised before 31 December 2026; after that date the article 86(3) common rate applies with penalties and late interest. [LFR 2026, art. 7](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcb8249c4ab_B%C3%A9nin-Loi%20de%20finances%20rectificative%202026.pdf#page=3) A declared dividend is not proof that undistributed-reserve or prior-tax-credit issues have been settled. Article 1 gives an income-period rule tied to the exercise closed 31 December 2025 unless otherwise stated. Do not infer the applicable income period merely from the signature date. [LFR 2026, art. 1](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcb8249c4ab_B%C3%A9nin-Loi%20de%20finances%20rectificative%202026.pdf#page=1) [LFR 2026, art. 3](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcb8249c4ab_B%C3%A9nin-Loi%20de%20finances%20rectificative%202026.pdf#page=2) [LFR 2026, art. 5](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcb8249c4ab_B%C3%A9nin-Loi%20de%20finances%20rectificative%202026.pdf#page=2) [LFR 2026, art. 6](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcb8249c4ab_B%C3%A9nin-Loi%20de%20finances%20rectificative%202026.pdf#page=3) [LFR 2026, art. 7](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcb8249c4ab_B%C3%A9nin-Loi%20de%20finances%20rectificative%202026.pdf#page=3)
6. LFR article 12 also addresses gains on securities of Benin-established enterprises regardless of seller/buyer residence, subject to treaties. LFR article 13 places the specified Benin-property rental-platform withholding on the platform owner, excluding operations for hotel establishments. Route these to their actual gain/rent calculation before payment; do not apply a dividend or service rule to them by analogy. [LFR 2026, art. 12](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcb8249c4ab_B%C3%A9nin-Loi%20de%20finances%20rectificative%202026.pdf#page=4) [LFR 2026, art. 13](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcb8249c4ab_B%C3%A9nin-Loi%20de%20finances%20rectificative%202026.pdf#page=4)

Read the interest tax event in article 85(2), including booked but unpaid interest, with article 91’s remittance rule; a cash-only calendar is insufficient. Article 91 requires remittance by the 10th of the month after the taxable products are put into payment; an approved dividend distribution uses the month of the approving meeting. LFR article 6 retains those limbs while adding the separate retained-profit deadline, so a cash payment date alone is insufficient for that special case. The accompanying monthly statement shows gross sums and tax. [CGI 2026, art. 90](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=49) [CGI 2026, art. 91](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=50) [LFR 2026, art. 6](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcb8249c4ab_B%C3%A9nin-Loi%20de%20finances%20rectificative%202026.pdf#page=3)

**Residence changes the ordinary dividend rate.** Assume an ordinary declared cash dividend of FCFA 1 million, no special reserve/retained-profit issue, no more favourable applicable treaty and no approved-listed-company condition. inputs:
  gross_dividend: 1000000
steps:
  nonresident_associate_tax: gross_dividend*0.05

  services: 1000000
steps:

  difference: without_separate_invoice-with_separate_goods_invoice

  difference: 800000

## The base

1. Reconcile monthly gross salary, overtime, bonuses and cash/benefit allowances, including transport, to the taxable components under article 122. Illness indemnities are included. [CGI 2026, art. 122](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=61)
2. Screen the actual exemptions in article 120 and exclusions in article 124. Statutory dismissal compensation is distinguished from taxable notice/leave compensation. Family social-security-type allowances have the article 120 cap condition; this is not a family-quotient deduction. Training and collective health insurance have their stated exclusions, and individual health cover has its own limit. Hold any exemption whose factual limit has not been evidenced. [CGI 2026, art. 120](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=60) [CGI 2026, art. 124](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=62)
3. Value benefits under article 123: actual value is the starting rule and the listed housing, domestic help, utilities, food and vehicles have statutory monthly valuations. Obtain the employee category, base salary and benefit details before applying that table. This Guide does not compute a benefit value from missing facts. [CGI 2026, art. 123](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=61)
4. Apply each band only to its slice of the resulting monthly base, then add the March/June levy when required. Do not multiply the monthly thresholds by twelve and apply them as a general personal annual scale. [CGI 2026, art. 122](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=61) [CGI 2026, art. 125](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=62)
5. Separate exceptional remuneration, including end-of-career amounts and thirteenth-month pay. Article 126 uses an average-salary method and special conditions; do not put an unresolved exceptional payment through the ordinary examples. [CGI 2026, art. 126](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=63)
## Deadlines and filing

The payer withholds when salary is paid and records each beneficiary, amount, date, nature of withholding and receipt reference. Put the tax on the payslip. Remit the monthly deductions by the 10th of the following month with the prescribed monthly declaration. [CGI 2026, art. 127](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=63) [CGI 2026, art. 128](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=64) [CGI 2026, art. 129](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=64)

A Benin-domiciled taxpayer paid by a foreign-established payer must make a spontaneous monthly salary declaration and payment on the same terms. The salary withholding is final under article 128(3); it is not a universal annual IRPP return for all income. An annual salary information statement remains due by 30 April under article 472, including its specified foreign-payer cases. [CGI 2026, art. 128](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=64) [CGI 2026, art. 472](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=204)

Prepare the payroll and monthly/annual summaries for the authorised filer. Authenticated DGI form fields, submission and payment acknowledgements were not accessed; this is not a completed payroll filing.
## Penalties and interest

General filing/payment sanctions and the conditional 2026 first-declaration relief are recorded once in the [overview](bj-tax-overview.md#penalties-and-interest). Assess the facts before using any relief. This working paper does not prepare a penalty assessment.
## Cross-border points

Record residence, work location, payer location and any treaty before accepting foreign payroll treatment. Foreign employment does not by itself remove a Benin-domiciled recipient from article 121. The company and foreign-service withholding rules are separate in the [cross-border Guide](bj-cross-border-withholding.md). [CGI 2026, art. 121](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=60) [CGI 2026, art. 128](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=64)
## Two worked examples that recompute

**Ordinary month.** Assume the taxable salary base, after evidenced statutory treatment, is FCFA 200,000 in an ordinary month. The first band is untaxed, the next slice gives 9,000 and the next gives 7,500, total ITS 16,500. No March/June levy arises.

```oa-check
name: Ordinary monthly ITS
inputs:
  salary_base: 200000
steps:
  band10: max(0,min(salary_base,150000)-60000)*0.10
  band15: max(0,min(salary_base,250000)-150000)*0.15
  band19: max(0,min(salary_base,500000)-250000)*0.19
  band30: max(0,salary_base-500000)*0.30
  its: band10+band15+band19+band30
expected:
  its: 16500
```

**June levy changes the amount.** A confirmed taxable base of FCFA 600,000 gives band tax of 101,500. It is above the first band, so the June levy adds 3,000. The withholding schedule totals 104,500. This example has no exceptional remuneration.

```oa-check
name: June ITS and levy
inputs:
  salary_base: 600000
steps:
  band10: max(0,min(salary_base,150000)-60000)*0.10
  band15: max(0,min(salary_base,250000)-150000)*0.15
  band19: max(0,min(salary_base,500000)-250000)*0.19
  band30: max(0,salary_base-500000)*0.30
  band_tax: band10+band15+band19+band30
  tax_plus_june_levy: band_tax+3000
expected:
  band_tax: 101500
  tax_plus_june_levy: 104500
```

## Who this applies to

Prepare the employer VPS schedule alongside the [salary ITS working paper](bj-income-tax.md). Persons paying salaries and accessory remuneration are within article 191, subject to article 192 exemptions. This Guide refreshes the tax side of payroll. It does not certify current CNSS contribution rates, ceiling, risk classification or remittance procedure: the official CNSS guidance failed to open, including in a normal browser. Do not compute a complete payroll cost or net salary while that social-security schedule is unresolved. [CGI 2026, art. 191](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=89) [CGI 2026, art. 192](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=89)

## The base

1. Reconcile employee taxable salary bases to the ITS schedule. VPS has the identical base; gross payroll without statutory classification is not an automatic substitute. [CGI 2026, art. 193](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=89)
2. For each line, establish the employer category and employee-specific exemption evidence. Record nationality, hiring date, first-employment evidence and CNSS declaration where article 192(3)–(4) is claimed. The domestic-employment exemption requires both CNSS declaration and payment. The sports/artists limit and trainee conditions must be established before any exclusion. [CGI 2026, art. 192](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=89)
3. Split the VPS base into ordinary, private-teaching and supported-exempt lines, then apply the appropriate rate only to the taxable category. Do not deduct VPS from the employee as an ITS withholding. The legal charge is on the person paying remuneration. [CGI 2026, art. 191](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=89) [CGI 2026, art. 193](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=89) [CGI 2026, art. 194](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=89)
4. Keep a separate CNSS schedule marked **not calculated** until current authoritative contribution bases, rates, risk category, ceilings and payment procedure are obtained. The old employer total omitted the separate injury-risk issue and cannot be reused as a verified all-in rate.
## Deadlines and filing

VPS is declared on the same declaration as ITS and paid on the conditions of articles 127–129, including the 10th of the following month. The annual salary information requirement is in article 472; retain employee and benefit details for it. [CGI 2026, art. 195](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=89) [CGI 2026, art. 129](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=64) [CGI 2026, art. 472](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=204)

Produce the employer tax schedule, exemption evidence and monthly declaration reconciliation for the authorised DGI filer. Authenticated fields and acknowledgements were not accessed. CNSS has its own unresolved declaration/payment process; no DGI date is copied into the CNSS schedule.
## Penalties and interest

General filing/payment sanctions and the conditional 2026 first-declaration relief are recorded once in the [overview](bj-tax-overview.md#penalties-and-interest). Assess the facts before using any relief. This working paper does not prepare a penalty assessment. CNSS sanctions are unverified and are not inferred from the tax code.
## Cross-border points

Nationality matters to the specific new-company/first-employment exemptions; it is not a blanket salary-tax or social-security exclusion. Foreign employment and residence belong in the salary Guide. # Benin annual property TFU working paper v0.1

## Who this applies to

Prepare a separate annual TFU ownership-tax working paper for property situated in Benin in 2026. A rental IRF computation is a different job, even when both appear on one assessment notice. [CGI arts151,104(3)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=74)

Classify permanently fixed constructions as built property. Uncultivated land used commercially or industrially is assimilated to built property. Light structures without masonry foundations are normally non-built, but income-producing or commercial light structures use the built regime. [CGI art152](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=74)

Start with the owner on 1 January, liable for the whole year. For usufruct use the usufructuary; for an emphyteutic lease use the lessee. For a building lease, the owner owes through the completion year and the tenant from the following year; keep the owner’s name after the liable person on the notice. [CGI art156(1)–(2)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=76)

If the owner cannot be reached, the possessor, agent, tenant, legatee or other successor pays on the owner’s behalf. If none is known, the administration can assess using the unique parcel number or another national/communal cadastral identifier; absence of the article598(1) particulars cannot by itself annul that notice. [CGI art156(3)–(4); LF2026 art15](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=76)

| TFU rate | For non-built property, use the commune’s applicable annual rate within the statutory 3%–7% range. | [CGI art159(1)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=77) |
| TFU rate | For built property, use the commune’s applicable annual rate within the statutory 4%–8% range. | [CGI art159(1)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=77) |

They are not verified universal 2026 rates. | [CGI art159(2)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=77) |
## The base

For built property, obtain the supported rental value under the ministerial methodology. Do not substitute purchase price, actual rent or a public-land sales-price schedule without the applicable valuation evidence. [CGI art157](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=76)

For non-built property, use the administrative assessment at 1 January. Municipal councils determine assessments from market values, revisable every five years. They notify DGI by 30 November before the end of each five-year period for values effective the following 1 January. If no values had been adopted when this provision commenced, a ministerial order sets the bases. [CGI art158](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=76)

Check the actual communal rate decision for the year, delivered to DGI by 30 November for the following 1 January. Where that notification is absent, article159(2) retains the preceding year’s rates. For valuation-period notification failure, article158(3) literally refers to the preceding quinquennium’s “taux”; do not invent a revised assessment from that wording. [CGI arts158(3),159(2)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=77)

Screen the article153 exemption classes: income-unproductive public property; diplomatic/international-organism property with a headquarters agreement; agricultural land and the specified agricultural uses; qualifying school/university/sport land; school/university buildings owned by the establishment; medical/social-assistance property; and worship property owned by the religious community. Record which exact class and factual conditions are met. [CGI art153](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=74)

Unsubdivided land sown, planted or replanted with trees of any species has the separate article155 exemption. Do not treat every vacant plot as exempt. [CGI art155](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=76)

New construction, reconstruction or extensions exclusively for the owner and family’s dwelling enter TFU in the fourth year following completion or first use. The exemption is only for the principal residence and only once for the same person. A later different use ends the remaining exemption from the year of conversion. [CGI art154(1),(3)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=75)

To claim that temporary exemption, send the tax service a letter with a building-permit copy and title proving ownership in the completion/first-use year, before the following 1 January. Existing-property TFU must be current. Without timely declaration, taxation starts permanently on 1 January of discovery. Do not grant relief from the construction date alone. [CGI art154(2)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=75)

After the liable person, property category, exemptions, lawful value and applicable local rate are supported, multiply the taxable value by that rate. Keep IRF and its ORTB levy outside this TFU multiplication. [CGI arts157–159;104(3)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=55)
## Deadlines and filing

Declare acquisition or completed construction to the tax service by simple letter within 30 days. Identify the parcel and full address, including the “Rue entrée de la parcelle” number; article161(2) requires a sign on non-built property or an inscription at the building entrance. Retain the letter and evidence of delivery. [CGI art161(1)–(2)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=77)

By 10 December each year, the owner or principal tenant, or property manager in their place, supplies a written occupancy statement: each tenant and let space, principal rent and charges; free occupants and space; owner-occupied space; vacant space. Inaccurate or missing information invokes article485. [CGI art161(3)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=78)

Prepare the TFU instalment schedule from the preceding year’s total: 50% by 10 February and the remaining 50% by 30 April. Reconcile the tax notice before settling any assessed balance; this Guide does not invent a first-year provisional amount without a prior assessment. [CGI art162](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=78)

Tenants/farm lessees pay TFU for the leased property on the owner’s behalf; the owner must accept the TFU receipt against the rent. Keep the receipt-to-rent reconciliation separate from IRF withholding to prevent two deductions for the same payment. [CGI art163](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=78)

Arrange mutation of the tax record on transfer. Until mutation occurs, the former owner remains assessed and can be pursued, with recourse against the new owner. Article165(2) requires the tax-certified TFU-current statement on acts granting/transferring ownership or use and the listed permits/titles. Tax receipts create the statutory presumption in article165(1), not a substitute for resolving a disputed title. [CGI arts164–165](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=78)

Prepare a dated packet with title/rights evidence, parcel identifier, property use, exemption evidence, the valuation instrument, local rate decision, previous assessment, occupancy letter and payment receipts. The statutory letter route is supported; authenticated DGI screens, field IDs, bank/payment-reference generation and acknowledgement were not accessed. Do not label the packet as a submitted return.
## Penalties and interest

For 1 January–31 December 2026, original finance-law article2 disapplies the specified TFU late increases, interest, command costs and seizure costs if all TFU principal due is paid and the landowner has an IFU. Obtain evidence of both conditions; do not extend this TFU measure to rental IRF or assume principal is forgiven. [LF2026 art2](https://budgetbenin.bj/storage/2025/12/Loi-des-finances-2026.pdf#page=2)

General sanctions are routed to the [overview](bj-tax-overview.md#penalties-and-interest). Determine the charge and relief conditions before paying; the specific TFU relief does not prove that every declaration penalty is waived.
## Cross-border points

TFU follows the Benin location of the property and the article156 rights-holder rules. A foreign address does not substitute for identifying the liable person. This working paper does not grant treaty relief or credit in another country. [CGI arts151,104(3)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=74) [CGI art156(1)–(2)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=76)
## Two worked examples that recompute

**Two categories, two bases.** Assume the commune’s actual 2026 decisions and valuation evidence have been supplied: a built building has assessed rental value FCFA1,200,000 and a 6% rate; non-built land has administrative value FCFA8,000,000 and a 5% rate. Neither is exempt. The rates are example facts within article159, not claimed national defaults. TFU is 72,000 and 400,000, total 472,000. No IRF or ORTB is included. [CGI arts157–159](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=76)

```oa-check
name: Separate built and nonbuilt TFU bases
inputs:
  built_rental_value: 1200000
  supported_built_rate: 6
  nonbuilt_assessed_value: 8000000
  supported_nonbuilt_rate: 5
steps:
  built_tfu: built_rental_value*supported_built_rate/100
  nonbuilt_tfu: nonbuilt_assessed_value*supported_nonbuilt_rate/100
  tfu_total: built_tfu+nonbuilt_tfu
expected:
  built_tfu: 72000
  nonbuilt_tfu: 400000
  tfu_total: 472000
```

**Principal-residence use changes the decision.** Assume a principal residence completed and first used in 2023, a timely valid exemption letter and all other article154 conditions. The fourth following year is 2027, so exclusive owner/family use would still be exempt in 2026. Instead the whole building is converted to a commercial letting in 2026: article154 ends the remaining exemption from that conversion year. With supported rental value FCFA900,000 and actual local rate 6%, the conditional 2026 assessment is 54,000 rather than zero. This is a use-change decision, not a month-by-month proration. [CGI art154](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=75)

```oa-check
name: Temporary residence exemption ends on changed use
inputs:
  completion_year: 2023
  rental_value: 900000
  supported_rate: 6
  qualifies_exclusive_residence: 0
steps:
  fourth_following_year: completion_year+4
  tfu_if_taxable: rental_value*supported_rate/100
  tfu_2026_after_conversion: tfu_if_taxable*(1-qualifies_exclusive_residence)
expected:
  fourth_following_year: 2027
  tfu_if_taxable: 54000
  tfu_2026_after_conversion: 54000
```

# Benin rental IRF and rent withholding working paper v0.1

> **General reference only.** This skill is general tax/accounting reference material for AI-assisted workflows. It has not been reviewed for any specific person's facts, documents, elections, deadlines, residency, filing status, or local procedures. Do not rely on it to file, pay, amend, or take a tax position without review by a qualified professional in the relevant jurisdiction.
## Who this applies to

Prepare a 2026 rental-income IRF and rent-withholding working paper, separately from annual TFU. IRF covers individuals and the article101(1) assimilated persons receiving property income: the State, communes, specified public establishments, associations and NGOs where they hold only property income. [CGI art101(1)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=54)

Partners of a property-predominant company not subject to IS enter IRF. For this chapter, more than 50% of company turnover must be article102 property income. A company subject to IS is not brought into the individual IRF computation merely because it owns a building. [CGI art101(2)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=54)

Article102 covers built and non-built property income, furnished letting, fixed industrial installations, building-lease rent and property-right ancillary income, only where the income is not included in business profits of an industrial/commercial enterprise, farm or noncommercial profession. Classify the business-income boundary first. [CGI art102(1)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=54)
## Rates, bands and thresholds

| Item | Rule and conditions | Official source |
|---|---|---|
| IRF or withholding branch | The IRF rate is 12% of the article103 taxable rental base. | [CGI art104(1)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=55) |
| IRF or withholding branch | The resulting IRF is increased by a separate FCFA4,000 ORTB levy. IRF and this levy appear distinctly on the same collection title as TFU; they are not a single combined percentage. | [CGI art104(2)–(3)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=55) |
| IRF or withholding branch | Tenant withholding is 12% of gross rent, reduced to 10% where the landlord is subject to IBA or IS. The 10% is a withholding classification, not a replacement individual IRF rate for every landlord. | [CGI art106(1)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=55) |
| IRF or withholding branch | Natural-person tenants are exempt from withholding, except those renting through an entity subject to tax on profits. Do not infer withholding exemption from a natural-person landlord. | [CGI art106(2)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=55) |
## The base

Start with gross rent. Add owner expenses contractually borne by the tenant, and subtract tenant expenses the owner paid for the tenant. Keep supporting contracts and invoices; the statute does not give this job a general percentage expense allowance. [CGI art103(1)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=54)

Owner-occupied housing has no imputed rental IRF under article102(2). By contrast, free provision to a third person without a legal obligation creates in-kind income valued under article157. The legal-obligation distinction must be evidenced before setting the imputed base to zero. [CGI arts102(2),103(2),157](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=55)

Prepare separate columns for gross rent paid, the adjusted article103 IRF base, the ORTB levy, withholding actually remitted and instalments. Article106(5) credits paid-and-remitted tenant withholding against tax due; article106(8) offsets withholding against instalments. A promise or unsupported deduction is not a paid-and-remitted receipt. [CGI art106(5),(8)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=56)

Article106(3) calls withholding final but keeps the annual declaration. Do not infer a general refund or merge the ORTB charge into withholding. For a landlord within IBA/IS, stop at the correct 10% withholding schedule and send final business-tax treatment to that tax’s working paper; the final-liability interaction is not computed here. [CGI art106(1),(3)–(5)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=55)
## Deadlines and filing

By 10 February annually, give the competent tax service a statement naming tenants, prior-year rent received and withholding suffered. Pay tax on income that was not withheld with that statement. The administration can directly determine the base from leases or property-survey information, with disputes under articles583 onwards. [CGI art105](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=55)

Remit withholding spontaneously by the 10th for the preceding month’s rent. If rent was paid in advance, withhold and remit by the 10th of the month following the actual advance payment; do not spread the remittance over the accommodation months. [CGI art106(4)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=55)

For State tenancies, Treasury deducts under article106(1) from rent-payment warrants and provides DGI a named prior-month withholding statement by the 10th. Owners remain jointly liable for remittance and can face the same recovery and sanctions. [CGI art106(6)–(7)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=56)

IRF uses four instalments as for IBA, which article66 pays as IS: provisionally one quarter of preceding-year tax by 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December. If the prior return is not filed by the first instalment, article51 uses the penultimate year provisionally, regularised at the second instalment. Offset supported withholding without duplicating it. [CGI arts106(8),66,51(1)–(2)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=56)

A non-IS property-predominant company files before 31 January: prior-year total receipts split between rent and other receipts, rent withholding, partners’ names/domiciles and their share counts. File at its registered-office tax service, or at the property-location service if the office is abroad. Pay unwithheld tax for partners with that statement. [CGI art107(1)–(2)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=56)

Partners still file the article105 statement but do not owe IRF again on their profit share to the extent the company has already paid it. Article107(4)–(5) sends inaccurate company information to article485 and places late declaration/remittance sanctions on the company. [CGI art107(3)–(5)](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=56)

Article66 expressly pays IBA as IS; article51 provides quarterly provisional amounts and dates. This cross-reference supports the IRF instalment timetable, not an invented universal 30-April IRF annual deadline. [CGI arts66,51](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=37)

Build the annual tenant list and property-company partner schedule from leases, cash/bank receipts and remittance evidence. Prepare the ordinary/advance-rent deduction register showing landlord tax status, tenant status, gross payment, rate, month, amount remitted and receipt. Reconcile annual liability, ORTB, withholding and instalments separately. Deliver the statements and payment schedule to the authorised filer. No authenticated DGI form, box, submission, payment-reference or receipt screen was accessed; those steps remain unfinished.

The [overview](bj-tax-overview.md#penalties-and-interest) owns general filing/payment sanctions. Apply the article106 owner joint-liability and article107 company reporting conditions above. The TFU-specific relief in original finance-law article2 must not be assumed to waive rental IRF charges. [LF2026 art2](https://budgetbenin.bj/storage/2025/12/Loi-des-finances-2026.pdf#page=2)

The June rectifying law adds CGI106(9): short/long accommodation bookings and rent collection for Benin buildings through Beninese or foreign electronic matching-platform operators enter article106(1) withholding, except operations for hotel establishments. ## Two worked examples that recompute

**Adjusted annual IRF base, with separate paid withholding.** An individual landlord outside IBA/IS receives FCFA2,400,000 rent. The tenant also pays 120,000 of the owner’s contractual costs; the owner pays 60,000 of tenant costs. Supported annual IRF base is 2,460,000, giving IRF 295,200. Add the separate ORTB 4,000. With valid paid-and-remitted withholding receipts totalling 288,000, the arithmetic reconciliation is 11,200 before any instalments. The example does not waive the annual statement or presume a refund. [CGI arts103–106](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=55)

```oa-check
name: Adjusted rental IRF and remitted credit
inputs:
  rent: 2400000
  owner_costs_paid_by_tenant: 120000
  tenant_costs_paid_by_owner: 60000
  remitted_withholding: 288000
  ortb: 4000
steps:
  irf_base: rent+owner_costs_paid_by_tenant-tenant_costs_paid_by_owner
  irf: irf_base*0.12
  assessment_with_ortb: irf+ortb
  cash_reconciliation_before_instalments: assessment_with_ortb-remitted_withholding
expected:
  irf_base: 2460000
  irf: 295200
  assessment_with_ortb: 299200
  cash_reconciliation_before_instalments: 11200
```

**An advance changes payment timing; status changes withholding.** On 5 May 2026 a non-exempt company tenant advances six months’ rent at FCFA150,000 monthly to an individual IRF landlord. Gross advance 900,000 creates 108,000 withholding, remitted by 10 June 2026, not monthly over six months. For an otherwise identical natural-person tenant renting directly without an intermediary profits-tax entity, article106(2) removes tenant withholding; it does not exempt the landlord’s IRF. If instead the landlord is demonstrably IS/IBA-subject, the same 900,000 payment produces 90,000 withholding at 10%, with final business tax outside this example. 1. Identify person/entity, legal form, activity, territory, period and actual documents before choosing a tax chapter. ## Two worked examples that recompute

**Known cash schedule, with an explicit boundary.** Hypothetical checked schedules all fall due in the same cash-planning month: IS balance 1,000,000, net VAT 180,000, salary ITS 16,500 and employer VPS 8,000. The identified DGI cash subtotal is 1,204,500. It excludes unresolved CNSS and any other unmapped liability, so it is not labelled total payroll/tax cost.

```oa-check
name: Known DGI cash schedule reconciliation
inputs:
  is_balance_due: 1000000
  net_vat_due: 180000
  salary_tax_due: 16500
  vps_due: 8000
steps:
  known_dgi_cash_subtotal: is_balance_due+net_vat_due+salary_tax_due+vps_due
expected:
  known_dgi_cash_subtotal: 1204500
```

**Do not pay a documented VAT amount twice.** Assume a checked VAT schedule shows gross net-of-current-input tax of 500,000 before a valid 100,000 withholding receipt and a valid prior credit of 50,000. Cash VAT is 350,000. A separate unexplained amount of 150,000 is held for evidence and is not deducted: deducting it would understate the cash schedule by 150,000. This case assumes the VAT Guide's legal and period gates are already met.

```oa-check
name: Supported offsets versus unresolved amount
inputs:
  vat_before_supported_offsets: 500000
  supported_withheld_vat: 100000
  supported_prior_credit: 50000
  unexplained_amount: 150000
steps:
  cash_vat: vat_before_supported_offsets-supported_withheld_vat-supported_prior_credit
  unsupported_comparison: cash_vat-unexplained_amount
  understatement: cash_vat-unsupported_comparison
expected:
  cash_vat: 350000
  unsupported_comparison: 200000
  understatement: 150000
```

# Benin transfer-pricing and reporting screen v0.2

> **General reference only.** This skill is general tax/accounting reference material for AI-assisted workflows. ## Who this applies to

Prepare a Benin cross-border related-party pricing and reporting screen in 2026. Article 45 allows indirect profit transfers through purchase/sale pricing or other means to be brought back into the accounts by comparison with independent conditions. Control includes majority capital/votes, actual decision power and common control. The dependence condition is not required for transfers to a privileged-tax-regime territory within article 30. No turnover safe harbour is inferred from the separate reporting thresholds. [CGI 2026, art. 45](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=28) [CGI 2026, art. 30](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=22)

## The base

1. Map counterparties, countries, legal/actual control and the transaction types. Screen privileged taxation against article 30 rather than treating an unrelated foreign supplier as automatically outside article 45. 2. Reconcile each controlled goods, services, finance and intangible transaction to contracts, invoices, accounts, quantities and actual functions. Identify a supportable independent comparison; record adjustments needed. This Guide does not invent an accepted margin from a benchmark not obtained. [CGI 2026, art. 45](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=28)
3. Test the annual declaration using the entity's own turnover OR gross assets and cross-border control condition. Test documentation separately: an entity below its own threshold can still be caught through the majority participation tests. [CGI 2026, art. 470](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=203) [CGI 2026, art. 543](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=239)

Check foreign-parent filing/exchange, designation and notified systemic failure under paragraphs 2–4 before concluding that a Benin subsidiary does or does not file. The current exchange list and operating instructions were not obtained; unresolved cases stay on hold. [CGI 2026, art. 471](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=203)
5. Produce a schedule listing counterparties, control evidence, jurisdiction, transaction totals, pricing evidence, own/group thresholds, annual-return decision, documentation decision and unresolved CbCR questions. Group/entity documentation does not replace invoices and individual supporting records. [CGI 2026, art. 543](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=239)
## Deadlines and filing

The annual declaration is electronic and due by 30 April; article 470 delegates its content/format to a ministerial order. CbCR is electronic within the separate period above and uses its own prescribed model. Obtain the actual current form/schema, applicable exchange list and portal acceptance evidence before filing. No authenticated fields or schema were accessed. [CGI 2026, art. 470](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=203) [CGI 2026, art. 471](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=203)

For audits, use the actual notice and the current law. LFR article 17 replaces the old on-site duration: two months where declared annual turnover does not exceed FCFA 2 billion, four months otherwise. For this test, declared annual turnover is the amount declared for any tax in any year under audit, including the current year; do not select only one favourable return or year. The four-month period can extend by four months for the listed technical/TP/exchange cases, with reasoned notice at least three days before expiry. This timing does not replace the separate article 542/543 document-response deadlines. [LFR 2026, art. 17](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcb8249c4ab_B%C3%A9nin-Loi%20de%20finances%20rectificative%202026.pdf#page=5) [CGI 2026, art. 542](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=238) [CGI 2026, art. 543](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=239)

Articles 470 and 471 refer to article 496. Its paragraph 6 describes a TP declaration but points to article 471, while article 470 is the annual TP declaration. This cross-reference needs legal confirmation before assigning a specific fixed fine to the annual return. Document the distinction rather than choosing an amount. Failure to provide audit documents also engages article 544 and the separate sanction provisions. [CGI 2026, art. 470](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=203) [CGI 2026, art. 471](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=203) [CGI 2026, art. 496](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=220) [CGI 2026, art. 544](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=239)

The pricing rule, annual return, audit documentation and CbCR are separate tests. A treaty or exchange arrangement must be checked on its own text. ## Two worked examples that recompute

**Reconcile a possible pricing adjustment.** Hypothetical controlled purchases comprise 1,000 units at FCFA 12,000 each. Assume a defensible comparable independent price of 10,000 per unit has already been established on equivalent terms. The indicated excess expense is 2 million, to be examined under article 45. This is not a pre-approved benchmark or automatic agreed adjustment.

```oa-check
name: Controlled purchase comparison
inputs:
  units: 1000
  charged_unit_price: 12000
  supported_comparable_price: 10000
steps:
  recorded_cost: units*charged_unit_price
  comparable_cost: units*supported_comparable_price
  candidate_profit_addback: max(0,recorded_cost-comparable_cost)
expected:
  recorded_cost: 12000000
  comparable_cost: 10000000
  candidate_profit_addback: 2000000
```

**The OR test changes the reporting decision.** A cross-border controlled Benin enterprise has VAT-exclusive turnover of FCFA 900 million and gross assets of 1.2 billion. Turnover is 100 million below the annual-declaration threshold but assets are 200 million above it. The asset limb is sufficient for article 470; do not average or add the two measures. CbCR remains a separate question.

```oa-check
name: Turnover OR asset threshold screen
inputs:
  turnover: 900000000
  gross_assets: 1200000000
  threshold: 1000000000
steps:
  turnover_shortfall: max(0,threshold-turnover)
  asset_excess: max(0,gross_assets-threshold)
expected:
  turnover_shortfall: 100000000
  asset_excess: 200000000
```

## The base

1. Reconcile every invoice to supply date, nature, place, taxable/exempt/zero-rate category and valid documentary support. Goods place rules are in article 233. Service place rules are in article 234 with the rectifying-law platform addition described below. For ordinary goods, the delivery/fact-generating event determines exigibility; for services, immovable works and the specified public contracts, it is receipt of the price, advances or deposits. Non-import advances make VAT due on that amount even before completion. Article 235 also prevents the fact-generating event falling after a total or partial invoice; resolve unusual timing before calculation. [CGI 2026, art. 233](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=112) [CGI 2026, art. 234](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=112) [CGI 2026, art. 235](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=113) [CGI 2026, art. 236](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=114)
2. The ordinary domestic base is the consideration received or receivable; import bases include the specified customs value and charges and exclude VAT itself. Genuine evidenced price reductions and exact reimbursed disbursements have article 240 conditions. Special margin bases and public-contract rules require separate review. [CGI 2026, art. 237](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=114) [CGI 2026, art. 238](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=115) [CGI 2026, art. 240](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=115) [CGI 2026, art. 242](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=116)
3. Deduct only qualifying business inputs, recorded and used for the business, with the required document: normalised invoice, import declaration and payment proof, self-supply declaration, or withholding receipt. The supplier must be liable for VAT. Check the right's timing; omitted deductions have the article 245 cut-off, and qualifying purchases at or above FCFA 100,000 before VAT require the specified non-cash payment methods. [CGI 2026, art. 243](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=116) [CGI 2026, art. 244](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=116) [CGI 2026, art. 245](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=116)
4. Apply exclusions before a mixed-use apportionment. Passenger/mixed-use vehicles and their services, fuel, lodging/reception and gifts have article 247 restrictions and exceptions. The qualifying industrial/BTP machinery fuel rule excludes tourism/passenger-transport vehicles; for BTP the eligible input deduction is limited to 90% of the VAT on the purchase invoice. Do not treat that as a general 90% rule for all business fuel. [CGI 2026, art. 247](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=117)
5. Directly allocate inputs to taxable and non-deductible activity first. Only common inputs use the article 249 ratio; exclude its specified transactions from the fraction, round the percentage up to the next whole unit, use the provisional prior-year/forecast ratio and regularise with the final ratio by 30 April of the following year. [CGI 2026, art. 248](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=118) [CGI 2026, art. 249](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=118)
6. Reconcile output VAT, eligible input VAT, withholding receipts and prior credit. Excess eligible deductions carry forward; a refund requires a qualifying article 253 case and article 254 documents/time limits, not an assumption that any credit is refundable. [CGI 2026, art. 252](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=120) [CGI 2026, art. 253](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=120) [CGI 2026, art. 254](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=121)

General filing/payment sanctions and the conditional 2026 first-declaration relief are recorded once in the [overview](bj-tax-overview.md#penalties-and-interest). A late nil/credit VAT declaration specifically incurs FCFA 50,000 per month or part month, capped at FCFA 500,000, under article 496(2). ## Cross-border points

For a non-domiciled supplier, article 262 requires a Benin representative; in its absence, the recipients/beneficiaries and specified billing/collection persons owe VAT and penalties. This is more conditional than an automatic reverse charge for every imported service. The place of the underlying service must first be established. [CGI 2026, art. 234](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=112) [CGI 2026, art. 262](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=124)

LFR article 14 adds platform place rules: online platform services follow the beneficiary's residence; online sales/service commissions are located in Benin where any specified operator, seller/buyer, provider/user is there at the transaction; property-related services follow the property's location. Article 258 separately charges operators with collecting/remitting the supply VAT and commission VAT and obtaining registration. Verify the exact transaction and avoid charging the same VAT twice through the operator and recipient. [LFR 2026, art. 14](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcb8249c4ab_B%C3%A9nin-Loi%20de%20finances%20rectificative%202026.pdf#page=4) [CGI 2026, art. 258](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcbd46ab83b_B%C3%A9nin-Code%20G%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20Imp%C3%B4ts%202026.pdf#page=123)

Platforms handling Benin property rentals also need the distinct rental-withholding assessment under LFR article 13, owned by the [cross-border Guide](bj-cross-border-withholding.md). A VAT result does not settle that withholding. [LFR 2026, art. 13](https://apisiteweb.impots.bj/media/6adcb8249c4ab_B%C3%A9nin-Loi%20de%20finances%20rectificative%202026.pdf#page=4)
## Two worked examples that recompute

**Ordinary taxable month.** Assume confirmed VAT status, no special base or withholding, FCFA 10 million of ordinary taxable consideration and FCFA 720,000 of fully eligible, evidenced input VAT. Output VAT is 1.8 million and net payable is 1.08 million.

```oa-check
name: Ordinary monthly VAT
inputs:
  taxable_consideration: 10000000
  eligible_input_vat: 720000
steps:
  output_vat: taxable_consideration*0.18
  net_vat: output_vat-eligible_input_vat
expected:
  output_vat: 1800000
  net_vat: 1080000
```

**BTP machinery fuel decision.** Assume the documented purchase qualifies specifically for the article 247 BTP machinery-fuel exception and is not for a passenger/tourism vehicle. VAT on the invoice is FCFA 180,000. The 90% limit allows 162,000; 18,000 is excluded. A full-credit comparison would overstate the deduction by 18,000.
